speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; to narrow this down, can you tell me if the skin lesions are itchy, painful, or have any specific shape like bull's-eyes or target-like spots?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That recent self-resolving knee pain sounds very much like a migratory polyarthralgia; given your camping trip in Minnesota, were you exposed to a tick bite or do you recall a deer tick? Also, have you noticed any rash spreading from your legs or trunk, or any joint swelling in your ankles or knees right now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Erythema Migrans with secondary tenosynovitis/arthritis). The history of migratory joint pain, Minnesota exposure, and the specific description of violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists are highly characteristic of late-stage Lyme disease, possibly mimicking an insect bite reaction or representing a specific cutaneous manifestation. Please proceed with testing for Borrelia burgdorferi antibodies (ELISA followed by Western Blot) and consider MRI of the wrist to rule out septic arthritis, although the migratory nature points strongly away from local infection.
